area: prooflog: editorial proofread of the activity log, its variants, the week chapters and the office announcer (src/copy/log.js, engine.js, pa.js; src/engine/audio/voice.js, director.js, tagmap.js), read as rendered in the frozen release build
summary: The log, the chapter lines and the announcer are in good order: 104,318 rendered lines from 1,320 seeded quarters hold no interpolation, sign, quote or final-stop error, all 39 announcer keys and 7 chapter lines match the copydeck word for word, and the chips of 28,715 action moves add up exactly to what the meters did. Eight things are worth a look: one real disagreement between the announcer and the manager's dialog, chips that break in mid-chip at common laptop and phone widths, two singular/plural slips inherited from the deck's own templates, three repetition or word-choice matters, and one nit.
verified_ok: Read all 588 rendered strings of log.js and pa.js in test-results/audit/strings.json (extract: test-results/audit/prooflog/strings-log-pa.tsv).

Read 19 whole seeded quarters line by line with each move's real meter changes beside the lines (balanced 11, 1, 3, 21; novice 3, 95; referral 1; caller 23; conference 3; risk 2; claink 5, 4, 13, 10, 93; claink-weekly 15; claink-budget 110; hail-only 5; emailer 109), three more with routine lines filtered out (mgr-farm 21, steady 1, expert 44) and six probe runs (spam-politics, spam-cadence, idle, ascend, broke, burn). Printouts: test-results/audit/prooflog/runs/*.txt (script playlogs.mjs).

Mechanical scan of 104,318 rendered lines from 1,320 quarters (22 policies x 60 seeds, scan.mjs, scan-out.txt): none with undefined / NaN / [object, a doubled space, '$-', an ASCII hyphen used as a minus, a straight quote, a '+−' sign, a missing final stop, a lowercase start, or more than 100 characters.

Chips tell the truth: over 28,715 action, Hail Mary and dialog moves (880 quarters, chips.mjs) the chips of the lines each move wrote add up exactly to what energy, stress, manager, reputation and product really did (0 disagreements; only a move that ends the run writes a line without chips). Clamped cases read correctly, e.g. 'Took a break. Exceptional nap (+38%).' with '+48 energy' and no stress chip at 0 stress.

Conditional wording matches state wherever it was reached: 'Rent charged.' only when cash went negative; 'The deal stays where it is.' only when the champion's deal was already at Closing; 'You brought something back from the conference.' only within a week of a conference; 'The rest of the forecast is not taking your calls.' only when deals walked; '$17,608 given in discounts' is 20% of list on a $70,432 close; the clAInk invoice repeats the run's own token and outcome counts.

Plurals correct at 0 / 1 / many for leads (cold calls, outreach, marketing, trending, stale, demo queue), deals (discovery, demos, lost, late-stage lost, reassigned at the QBR), introductions (favors), contracts, outcomes, dead leads and potential customers.

Week chapters: the seven lines match copydeck section 6 word for word, are drawn under the week they announce (4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12, 13), and agree with the rules (reviews from week 5, dismissal from week 6). close.nobody uses the right chapter's wording in weeks 1-3, 4-6, 7-9 and 10-13.

Announcer: all 39 keys match copydeck section 9 word for word (deckcheck.mjs). In the release build the caption is the spoken line, typeset: speech engine handed "Pipeline hygiene is everyone's responsibility.", caption 'PA Pipeline hygiene is everyone’s responsibility.'; same for a week turn ('Marketing leads delivered. Qualification remains your responsibility.'). After a failed clAInk run the warning dialog correctly hides the caption that would repeat its body (warning-plain.png).
The engine's promise holds: no variant line was written word for word twice running in any quarter; the same seed renders the same log.

Log copy matches copydeck sections 4 and 5 (320 distinct rendered sentences checked; the only departures are the deck's own conditional alternatives: 'You found N potential customers', 'no deals qualified', and the truthful 'The deal stays where it is.').

Typography is consistent between neighbouring lines: true minus (U+2212) in chips and money, curly quotes and apostrophes, lowercase after 'Label:', American spellings (canceled, rumored, color-coded), 'one-to-one'.

Seen and left alone (deliberate, approved, or below the bar): 'Discovery: 0 deals qualified.' followed by 'Discovery: no deals qualified.' (the deck's fallback, recorded in docs/2.1/copy-coverage-notes.json L206); the same trip approved twice running ('Management approved your trip to Cancun.' in consecutive weeks: 20% of second approvals, five destinations; would need a rules change); ck.strike.hurt lines carry no chips, so a churn strike's clawback appears only on the strike card (as the deck's row has it, unchanged since 2.0.1); 'The badge still works. You have a new improvement plan.' directly followed by 'The improvement plan is no longer necessary. No one explains why.' (mgr-farm 21 week 13; 3 of 2,640 quarters); 'Commission $X.' without a colon in close.signed variant B (verbatim from the deck); cash is placed after the first chip, so a quad shot drunk at 100 energy reads '+15 stress · −$6' (only at full energy); week 12's 'One week remaining.' (deck says keep the 5/7/12/13 mapping).

findings.title: After a clAInk run that worked, the announcer speaks and captions the failure quip under the manager's dialog
findings.where: Dialog ck:warning when params.miracle is true. src/engine/audio/tagmap.js:62 (MODAL_SAY 'ck:warning' -> 'chatgdp'), src/copy/pa.js:63 (LINES.chatgdp), src/ui/Game.jsx:170 (onModal is given the id only), src/ui/primitives.jsx:50 (a caption is hidden only when it repeats the dialog's body), src/copy/claink.js:169 (CK_QUIP has both openings).
findings.evidence: Release build, policy claink seed 5, week 2 (save test-results/audit/prooflog/save-claink5-w2-predeploy.json, press Run agents; script warning.cjs). The dialog 'Writing development opportunity' shows, under its title, the caption 'PA Always on ChatGDP, huh?' and, as its body, '“Nice week. ChatGDP do that? Enjoy it. I’d like you to develop your own written communication skills before I start intervening in your deals.”'. The speech engine is handed 'Always on Chat GDP, huh?'. The log line reads '“Nice week. ChatGDP do that?” Your manager has issued a writing warning.' Picture: test-results/audit/prooflog/warning-miracle.png. Control after a failed run (claink seed 4, week 2): body '“Always on ChatGDP, huh? That’s not writing. …”', no caption, same spoken line (warning-plain.png). Frequency: 27 of 93 first warnings in 1,320 quarters (29%). Copydeck section 10 says of the manager's lines: 'These must match modal and actual event.' Related, from the code only (never reached in 2,640 quarters): src/ui/ClainkUi.jsx:391 says the same line for the 'ChatGDP again? We’ll circle back.' case.
findings.proposal: Give the spoken line its second approved opening. Add LINES.chatgdpNice = ["Nice week. Chat GDP do that?"] in src/copy/pa.js (CK_QUIP(true) in the spoken spelling; captionOf already typesets 'Chat GDP'); pass the dialog's params to the director (Game.jsx:170 a.onModal(shownId, shown.params); director.js onModal(id, params) -> say(line, {cooldown:4000, meta:params})); and in voice.js say(), beside the existing fired/repo remaps: if(key === "chatgdp" && opts.meta && opts.meta.miracle) key = "chatgdpNice". The dialog's own rule then hides the caption, exactly as it does after a failed run. Smaller still: say nothing when params.miracle is true.
findings.risk: One new key in LINES: the copy lint and test/audio enumerate keys, and section 9 of the deck has no row for it (the words are the deck's own, sections 7 and 10), so it wants the editor's nod. onModal's second argument is optional, so test/audio/behaviour.test.mjs and other callers keep working. No rules, saves or dice are touched.

findings.title: Stat chips break in the middle of a chip, and the wrapped row loses its alignment
findings.where: Activity panel and the phone peek. src/styles/app.css:154-156 (.line .body, .line p, .line .deltas) and src/copy/log.js:27-32 (fx joins chips with ' · ' and ordinary spaces). Worst on LOG["act.politics"], LOG["evt.security.own"], LOG["act.conference"] with the bonus, and on phones LOG["evt.caseStudy"].
findings.evidence: Release build, measured with wraps.cjs. 1366x768 (Activity 530px, row 474px) and 1280x720 (496 / 440px): politics chips render '−20 energy · +2 stress · +8 manager · −4 reputation · +3' / 'product'; security disclosure '+6 reputation · −18 product · −15 pp signing odds for 2' / 'weeks'; conference '−40 energy · −$800 · +5 stress · +8 pp signing odds this' / 'week'. The broken row starts at the left edge while one-row chips sit at the right. The politics row breaks at every desktop width from 1025px to about 1430px (measured at 1100, 1200, 1280, 1366, 1400, 1420; it fits at 1440). Phones: 390x844 '… +8 manager · −4' / 'reputation · +3 product' and '+5 reputation · +8 pp signing odds next' / 'week'; 360x740 starts a row with the separator ('· −4 reputation · +3 product'). Pictures: test-results/audit/prooflog/act-conf3-1366x768.png, act-claink5-1366.png, act-claink5-390.png. Tried in the page only (wrapfix.cjs): with no-break spaces inside each chip and text-align:right on .deltas, breaks fall only between chips ('… −4 reputation ·' / '+3 product'), nothing overflows from 320 to 1440px (fix-claink5-1366x768.png).
findings.proposal: Keep each chip whole: where fx() and pp() build the string, join the words inside a chip with U+00A0 and keep the ordinary space after each '·' (plus the few hand-written dl strings: evt.competitor.match, evt.freeze, week.fullFunnel, week.neglected, pay.repoWarn, act.crm.nuked); add text-align:right to .line .deltas so a second row stays under the first. Optional in the same pass: .line p{text-wrap:pretty} removed every one-word last line in the trial ('… Nobody asked which' / 'roadmap.', '… refer to this as a' / 'strategy.', '… The subject line contains' / '“FINAL.”') at 360-1440px; browsers without it ignore it.
findings.risk: dl is stored in saves and read by tests: anything that parses chips by splitting on a plain space (scripts/lint-copy.mjs, test/engine/copy.test.mjs's plain(), the strings snapshot) must treat U+00A0 as a space, and golden 'full' digests change (words only; 'mech' must not). A chip can no longer wrap inside itself: the longest, '−15 pp signing odds for 2 weeks' (31 characters), still fit a 320px phone in the trial. Doing it in markup instead (one nowrap span per chip in Activity.jsx and LogPeek.jsx) leaves stored text alone but changes the DOM the layout tests see. Chromium only was available.

findings.title: A single referral is described as “One of them”
findings.where: LOG["act.network"], src/copy/log.js:105 (the suffix is appended whatever n is). Copydeck section 4 row act.network gives the suffix with no singular form.
findings.evidence: Rendered in the release build: 'Referrals: 1 introduction. One of them is a whale.' (risk seed 2, week 4; picture test-results/audit/prooflog/act-whale-n1.png) and 'Referrals: 1 introduction. One of them is substantial.' (risk seed 2 week 1; claink-weekly seed 15 week 1). Over 1,650 quarters (measure.mjs): 319 of 1,074 suffixed referral lines have n = 1 (29.7%; 4.4% of all 7,172 referral lines), including 87 of 289 whale announcements, the line the announcer also marks with 'Large opportunity detected.' The deck's own rule (section 1): 'Use zero/one/many forms.'
findings.proposal: When n is 1, say the suffix in the singular: ' It is a whale.' / ' It is substantial.' Same claim, no new joke; two-plus introductions keep the approved wording.
findings.risk: Words only: golden 'full' digests change. The sonar sound and the announcer read params.size, not the sentence; no test or code matches this text (grepped).

findings.title: “1 of your largest deal”
findings.where: LOG["evt.rebalance"], src/copy/log.js:181; the rule takes up to two deals and one when one is all there is (src/game/events.js:141-151). The singular comes from the deck's template '{n} of your largest {deal/deals}'.
findings.evidence: Rendered in the release build: 'Territory optimization: 1 of your largest deal, $10,157, reassigned.' (hail-only seed 5, week 2; picture test-results/audit/prooflog/act-rebalance-n1.png). Rare: it needs manager under 35 and exactly one open deal (3 quarters of 2,640, all hail-only; none in the seven core policies).
findings.proposal: Keep the noun plural after 'of your largest' whatever n is: `${p.n} of your largest deals, ${usd(p.value)}, reassigned.` ('1 of your largest deals' is correct English; '2 of your largest deals' is unchanged.)
findings.risk: Words only (golden 'full' digests). LOG["qbr.reassigned"] ('reassigned 1 deal worth …') is correct and should stay as it is.

findings.title: Avoiding a repeat always lands on the first alternative, so its joke returns every other time
findings.where: src/copy/engine.js:56 (the shift walk) with mostly() in src/copy/log.js:23 ([plain, plain, plain, A, B]). Most visible on LOG["pay.salary"]; also LOG["act.politics"], LOG["coffee.shot"] shot 1, the zero-result lines of act.propose / act.demo / act.discovery.
findings.evidence: From any of the three plain slots the walk reaches variant A before B, so after a plain line a second plain pick always becomes A. Measured over 1,650 quarters (11 policies x 150 seeds, measure.mjs): pay.salary plain 'Payroll deposited.' 41.8%, variant A 'Salary deposited. HR has confirmed your continued existence.' 36.6%, variant B 'Payroll cleared.' 21.7% (n = 17,565). The HR line appears 3 to 6 times in every completed quarter (mean 4.81 of 13 Fridays, 809 quarters) and 60.3% of its consecutive appearances are exactly two weeks apart (emailer seed 109: weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12). act.politics 40.8 / 34.8 / 24.4%; coffee.shot #1 43.7 / 35.1 / 21.2%; act.propose with nothing advanced: A 594 against B 390 (referral seed 1, week 8: 'No proposals sent. The pricing spreadsheet survives another day.' / 'Proposals sent: 0.' / the same joke again). Lines whose numbers vary sit near the intended mix (act.prospect 56.5 / 22.3 / 21.1). The deck (section 5) asks for the base row 'approximately 60% of the time' and variants 'sparingly'; log.js:15-17 says 'about three times in five'.
findings.proposal: In render(), when the pick repeats lastText, choose among the other distinct wordings by the hash instead of taking the next one in list order (about four lines). Simulated against the shipped algorithm in test-results/audit/prooflog/variant-sim.mjs: plain 42.7%, A 28.6%, B 28.7%, still never the same sentence twice running. A stronger option (let the plain line follow itself, alternatives may not) gives 63.7 / 16.7 / 19.6 but breaks the promise test/engine/copy.test.mjs asserts and would let close.nobody's plain line, itself a joke, repeat: not recommended.
findings.risk: Every seeded run reads differently from its first avoided repeat on, so golden 'full' digests and anything that pins msg text need regenerating; 'mech' digests and the dice are untouched (the choice rolls nothing). Logs already stored in saves keep their text. Whether a move from 36.6% to about 29% clears the studio's bar is an editorial call.

findings.title: “Exceptional nap” is the usual nap
findings.where: LOG["act.recharge"], src/copy/log.js:107; what counts as worth a mention is decided at src/game/actions.js:149 (luck >= 0.15 of a 0-0.5 roll).
findings.evidence: 70.3% of 16,886 recharge lines in 1,650 quarters read 'Took a break. Exceptional nap (+N%).'; the plain 'Took a break.' is the exception (29.7%). balanced seed 3: 11 of 13 recharges are 'Exceptional'; balanced seed 1: weeks 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 13. In 2.0.1 the same condition printed 'Good nap, +N%.'; the deck changed the adjective ('nap positive: Exceptional nap (+{nap}%).') but not the condition. The hint bar calls the 20% trip roll 'A rare great nap'.
findings.proposal: Print the suffix only at the top of the range, on the copy side: `p.nap >= 35` in log.js:107 (about three recharges in ten). The rules and d.nap stay as they are.
findings.risk: Words only (golden 'full' digests). test/copy/render.mjs feeds nap 19 and would stop exercising the suffix (it asserts nothing about it); the lint sample in log.js already uses nap 42. The exact cut is the editor's to choose.

findings.title: The no-repeat check is blind when only an account name or a source label differs
findings.where: src/game/log.js:36 (lastText is the previous line's whole sentence) with src/copy/engine.js:56; LOG["close.nobody"] and LOG["deal.ghost"].
findings.evidence: close.nobody: 'Close push: no signatures. Verbal enthusiasm remains strong.' directly followed by 'Friday closes: no signatures. Verbal enthusiasm remains strong.' (steady seed 1, week 3; claink seed 93, weeks 9-10): 341 of 3,006 consecutive pairs (11.3%) in 1,650 quarters repeat the previous punchline, all under another label. deal.ghost on one Friday: 'Neon Narwhal has described silence as its preferred next step.' / 'Ghost Pepper Labs has described silence as its preferred next step.' (novice seed 8, week 8; expert seed 44, week 13 has three in a row): 73 of 171 neighbouring pairs (42.7%), in 65 of 1,650 quarters (ghost.mjs).
findings.proposal: Before the comparison, put the new line's account or source label in place of the old one's in lastText (three lines at log.js:36, using e.d.account / e.d.src and CLOSE_SOURCE), so the same wording about another account counts as the same wording and the engine moves to the next variant.
findings.risk: Words only (golden 'full' digests); nothing mechanical. If src/game is frozen for 2.1.1, the same substitution can live in render() by handing it the previous line's params. Best regenerated together with the previous finding.

findings.title: The last Friday still quotes next week's signing odds
findings.where: LOG["week.neglected"], LOG["week.fullFunnel"], LOG["evt.caseStudy"], LOG["evt.freeze"] (src/copy/log.js:176-187); src/game/week.js writes them in week 13 before the QBR ends the run.
findings.evidence: 766 of 809 completed quarters (94.7%) end with a week-13 line whose chip reads '−6 pp signing odds next week' or '+6 pp signing odds next week', two to five lines above the verdict. balanced seed 1: 'Parts of your funnel have been declared a nature reserve. [−6 pp signing odds next week]' / 'Q1 final: 150% of quota.' / 'QBR: leadership applauds the territory’s potential.' / 'President’s Club. …'. There is no next week. It sits dimmed behind the ending dialog (test-results/audit/prooflog/end-balanced21.png), so few players will read it.
findings.proposal: Leave alone unless these lines are being touched anyway. If they are: drop the chip when the line is written in week 13; the line functions already receive the week, e.g. (p, c) => line(text, c.week >= 13 ? "" : chip).
findings.risk: Words only. The effect the rules add in week 13 is never used and can stay.

not_checked: Audible speech: headless Chromium has no voices, so I compared the text handed to speechSynthesis.speak with the caption, not the sound. Only Chromium exists here, so line breaking and text-wrap support in Safari and Firefox are unverified.

Lines no simulated quarter produced were read only as strings, not in sequence: act.recharge.flat (needs six shots in a five-slot week), evt.pipShred, qbr.pipUp and qbr.dodgedUp (need a PIP before the QBR, which a one-quarter run cannot have), ck.mgr.circle, ck.dismiss (the bots never dismiss the ad), end.fired.politics, end.meltdown.stress.

clAInk's workspace report and strike cards, the ending cards and cutscene captions, the hint bar and the handbook: other audits' material, touched only where the announcer or the log meets them. One thing noticed in passing for the endings audit: 'Distinction earned: Whale hunter.' was logged after a Friday close (novice 95, week 9) and after a Hail Mary (risk 2, week 4), while the card calls it 'a single qualifying close push'.
Screen-reader output of the log (aria-live) and which lines the phone peek chooses to show.
Logs inside old saves: they keep their 2.0.1 wording by design and were not proofread.

That the frozen build equals HEAD: assumed from a clean tree at 78bfc3f and from finding the four templates in question in test-results/audit/build/release.html. The simulations ran on a snapshot of src/game and src/copy taken at the start (test-results/audit/prooflog/engine), unchanged when I finished.
Humour and voice beyond errors: no joke was judged on taste, and no alternative wording is offered anywhere above except the two singular forms.
